channel.title: House on Schank Farm
channel.description: Recent content in House on Schank Farm

item.title: Japanese Beetles
item.description: Keith wrote that it’s been really hot and dry, and they’ve had almost no breaks from irrigation, but the crops that have been getting water look pretty good. Luckily we have a very high water table under our farm.

item.title: Planting roses & landscaping
item.description: The house and lawn have come a long way in the past two years. Dad and my brother Jeff have fertilized the lawn regularly, and I planted small bushes including Goldflame Spirea around the house. Dad and Jeff also planted a little orchard of fruit trees (apple, cherry, peach) in the north and east lawns.

item.title: Farmhouse upgrades underway
item.description: We pulled out the old overgrown bushes, added dirt and rock around the house, upgraded the sprinkler irrigation system, pulled out the old broken cement porches and sidewalks, poured new sidewalks and built new wood porches, put on new doors, and (after this photo), put on a new roof. Whew! See also photos of the original homestead in 1875 and this house when it was built in 1949.

item.title: Little red pump house
item.description: Keith ordered some iron, and he and his dad built a replacement shed for the south well. Before building, we talked about colors and decided red with white trim would be cute. (Red is the Swedish way.) They did an awesome job! Dad says it’s the best looking pump house in the county.

item.title: The Farm and House in 1949
item.description: Courtney, who (with her husband) rents our house, shared some photos with me from her mom’s photo album from 1949! Small world: Courtney is the great granddaughter of Alfred Kohtz, who Dad bought the house and farm from in the early 1960’s. That’s why Courtney so wanted to live here, and contacted us when she learned from her uncle Lowell that we planned to rent out the house.**
